page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.16xlarge is a storage-focused instance type within the Local SSDs family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 33 MB of L3 cache, 256 GB of system RAM, and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. It features 7679 GB of bundled local SSD storage and contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation reveals distinct execution trade-offs between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance metrics, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 966.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 18.97 GB/sec, fall into lower performance tiers due to the conservative base clock frequency. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded execution reaches solid median benchmarks, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 46759.09 and a PassMark CPU score of 38203.37. Memory throughput maintains consistent middle-tier results, transferring 118.82 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.43 GB/sec for writes.

The inclusion of substantial local SSD capacity alongside a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides resource density tailored for data storage pipelines. Rather than paying separately for detached high-IOPS block storage volumes, the integrated disk space delivers cost efficiency for input-output heavy workloads that do not require state-of-the-art per-core compute speeds. Appropriate use cases include distributed database clusters, NoSQL datastores like Redis, caching layers, log aggregation, and large-scale data ingestion.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.16xlarge is an x86_64 instance type from the Local SSDs family designed for storage-intensive and data-centric workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the configuration delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 256 GB of RAM, and 7679 GB of bundled local SSD storage, with a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps and no GPUs. Benchmark metrics demonstrate moderate multi-core throughput alongside lower-tier single-threaded compute, reflecting its architectural prioritization of parallel execution and storage density over high individual core speeds. The integrated local solid-state storage provides efficient local I/O handling without the overhead of external network-attached volumes. This instance profile is well aligned with distributed databases, caching tiers, log indexing systems, and parallel data processing jobs requiring co-located disk capacity.
